campaign: Integrated validation, phase 2: bounded capability gains and evidence-gated simplification
doctrine:
overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data, promote or revert), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The milestone is the loop itself (improvement-loop): from there, the scorecard's gaps generate the work. Progress is counted in promotions, not landings: a cycle that measured, trained or changed, judged on held-out data and moved main. Until a cycle has promoted, rows that close the cycle rank above rows that only harden or slim it.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing owner and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing owner can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced, and a run leaves its evidence complete by its own contract (every protocol a suite's acceptance asks for), never half-written for a later landing to trip on.

The landing gate judges the commit; the improvement cycle judges the models. The gate's verdict depends only on the tree: unit, golden, hermetic-fixture and small-device checks. Suites that load real models, read the live store's evidence or sweep the device belong to the cycle, declared by build tag, and promotion of main requires them on the commit it promotes; a store write never changes a landing's verdict. A change's landing cost is read from its diff as three independent effects: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost, so false lane reach is cut. A surface move also expires every evaluation bound to the surface, so the re-evaluation it forces counts in its cost: surface changes are batched and land before an evaluation run, never between its runs, and the guards are re-acquired once after the last of them. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a user-facing result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract, whether it moves to the cycle or is deleted; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

A step's verify fails before the change and passes after; a verify that already passes proves nothing, so a boundary is proved by the table row that fails today. Before a landing, what the gate refuses cheaply is run locally first: the claims check after any hand edit, the invariant tables, the rules' budget and exports, and the step's verify. A refusal found after the lanes costs an hour, and a retried landing rebuilds an identical gate binary.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the owner reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

Landing speed is protected by observing it, not by a rule. Each structural boundary (a changed path's lanes, a package kept off the inference surface, a suite kept to the cycle) is pinned as an invariant row in one table per kind, never as a new test function or a snapshot of today's lists. At each periodic review the gate's measured lines in git log are read: the share of landings that reached no lane, lane minutes per landing, and executed versus cached package counts. A rise means a misplaced check or a new false reach, fixed by moving it and adding a table row. There are no time budgets or timeouts, no ratchet baselines, and no separate tracking subsystem.

Training research is measured at the lowest cost that answers the question, reusing what exists. Optimizer math stays on the device: host Muon on the tied embedding cost about 98 s a step, and moving it took a 540-step run from about 21 hours to 6 minutes. During training only scalars cross to the host (losses, norms, brake decisions), never weights or gradients per step. Reuse comes before acquiring: cached base losses keyed by the exact window plan, existing checkpoints, held-out sets and the verdict code, before any new dataset, pass or tool. An evaluation beats a training run, a norm beats a decomposition, and a one-time computation beats a per-step one. For a training rate question the order is: post-hoc tests on existing checkpoints, then the held-out brake from the training forward against cached base losses, then a per-layer relative step size, and per-direction spectral scaling last.

items.title: Measure whether a per-step relative Muon rate transfers across models

steps.title: Measure whether a per-step relative Muon rate transfers across models
steps.rationale:
Owner proposal 2026-10-02: derive Muon's rate per layer from the layer, a per-step relative size rho*||W||/||U||, with a held-out brake (paired against the base's per-window loss) and no first-step line search (the 200-window sweep showed the short horizon favours the rate that later drifted). Measured: relative movement over 540 steps scales linearly with the rate; the good run moved matrices 0.8-1.4% (about 2.4e-5 per step), the old rate 6-10%; equal total movement is not equal outcome; 1-D norms and biases move 50-100x less relatively (tmp/relative_movement.go). On Qwen2.5-0.5B matrix weight scales differ at most 1.5x, so the per-layer rule cannot be told from the exponent there. Step: calibrate rho on 0.5B in the scratch sweep harness, then measure a second model; add its measured band as a row of TestDerivedRateFineTunesMeasuredModels; adopt the per-layer rule only if it transfers where the exponent does not; measure the 1-D tensors separately. Serves: train.

Post-hoc evaluation 2026-10-02 (no training; the good run's change, held-out 56 records, host log loss; scratch train3-wt zz_projection_eval_test.go): base 2.5508 (accuracy 0.4936); full change 2.3038 (0.5143, 56/56 records improve); inside W's row and column spaces 2.3913 (65% of the gain); singular-value part 2.5496 (none); rotation part 2.3913; outside W's spaces only 2.2933 (0.5171, beats the full change); full change except q and o 2.2964; q and o only 2.4966. Paired, removing the q/o change: Hodges-Lehmann -0.0074 nats, block-bootstrap 95% [-0.0086, -0.0066], 55/56 records improve. Conclusions: the learning lives mostly in the rectangular layers and outside their current spaces, so the subspace-restricting spectral rules are dropped, and so is the singular-value-only rule; the square attention matrices' update, where weak directions moved 100-240x more than strong ones, slightly hurts in combination. Per layer kind the drifting run's excess was uniform (6.9-7.5x against a 7.35x rate), but within kinds q/k/v relative movement spreads up to 6x across layers. Next arms on the device, paired held-out log loss, replicated on a second model: plain Muon at parameters^-0.6; q and o at a damped relative step; spectral scaling on q and o only if damping helps.

items.title: Close the measured decode and load gaps: Unlimited-OCR decode first

budget.reason: the routed-expert node becomes three launches over a per-token scratch with token grouping (launch_moe.go, the scratch reservation in executor.go) and the loader keeps rank-3 bf16 expert banks raw a layer at a time (runner_weights.go); bought: Unlimited-OCR decode 3.94 to 88.2 tok/s and 4.5 GiB less device memory at identical outputs

steps.title: Load a model in one pass: hash while uploading
steps.rationale: Owner analysis 2026-10-02: load is 21.7-31.1 s for the large models; the about 12 s re-hash on gemma-12B is an extrapolation, not a measurement. Measure first: a per-phase load breakdown (header, hash, read, upload, other) for gemma-12B, Qwen3.8-27B and E4B. Then the single-pass load: hash the bytes as they upload and refuse to serve on a mismatch, which keeps integrity (trusting a size and mtime memo instead was declined). Serves: inference (load-time).

steps.title: Decode Bonsai's 1-bit weights in register
steps.rationale: Bonsai-27B Q1_0 decodes at 33.2 tok/s, about 13 percent of its bound: prefill is batched, decode is per-vector. Measure the decode step's kernel breakdown first, then a dequantize-in-register decode kernel that keeps each dot's order so outputs stay bit-identical and replay carries its evaluations. Serves: inference (throughput).

steps.title: Measure where E4B and gemma-12B decode time goes, and whether the non-native fp8 variant still serves anything
steps.rationale: gemma-4-E4B decodes at about 40 percent of its bound and gemma-4-12B fp8-native at about 50; kernel breakdowns name the next fix or close the gap as bandwidth-bound. gemma-4-12B-it-fp8 (non-native) is slower, heavier and slower to load than the native file at equal held-out quality (31.1 tok/s, 31.1 s, 22.5 GiB against 41.5, 22.6 s, 14.7 GiB; 0.4919 against 0.4926): ask the owner whether it still serves anything before spending device time on it. After the routed-expert fix Unlimited-OCR's routed layer is still 6.4 times the dense feed-forward of the same weight volume (0.94 ms against 0.15 ms); the warp-per-row shape would close that but reorders sums, so it changes MoE outputs and needs its evaluations re-run. Serves: inference (throughput).

items.title: Record the load phase of every capability the cycle measures

steps.title: Record the load phase of every capability the cycle measures
steps.rationale: Scorecard at 5455dc909: load-time is unmeasured on 20 rows and peak-device-memory on 18, nearly every non-inference capability, and six rows have no serving attempt; the twelve scorecard-unmeasured-* rows the loop proposed are these cells by task, and they close as their gaps close. Root causes (scratchpad measure-cells.md, 2026-10-03): recipe measure records a WholeOutput attempt that carries no phases (cmd/recipe/main.go:482-502; internal/servingattempt/servingattempt.go:25-32), and the load boundary sits inside each executor. This step, built (measure-cells.patch, reworked after review to half its first size): capabilityruntime times its own two load call sites (runtime.go, session_director.go) and carries the wall in the Measured value it already returns, cmd/recipe passes it into the attempt, and servingattempt writes it as the load phase; every catalog executor but vqa records one, and a request a resident session serves records zero. No pinned or inference-root path is touched, but capabilityruntime is in the evaluation and training closures, so benchmark and training-proof records read as moved and the next cycle re-acquires them (replays and six proofs): land it in the same window as the decode surface batch. After landing, run the sixteen recipe measure commands in the notes once (the cells are current by receipt, so no cycle re-runs them): 16 load cells fill and four rows get their first attempt. Serves: measure and find the gap (load-time).

steps.title: Record a measured capability's peak device memory from one process-wide ledger
steps.rationale: No honest per-attempt peak exists outside two video runtimes: capabilityruntime asks the loaded model for PeakDeviceBytes (measured.go:44-52), only Wan and LiveEdit implement it, and Wan still records 0 because its sessions read their statistics through the stage's cancelled context (latentvideo/runtime.go:135-136). Allocation accounting is per driver.Library (internal/cuda/driver/driver_windows.go:584-601), one per worker. One mechanism for every task: a process-wide current and peak beside accountAllocation and accountFree with an accessor, read by recipe measure for its one process and one attempt; it also corrects LiveEdit, whose 3.04 GiB is the larger of two sessions resident together (hypothesis, measure). internal/cuda is a pinned media runtime path and moves every surface, so this lands with a reviewed delta in a surface batch (the decode batch of inference-decode-gaps is the natural one). Nine of the eighteen rows run on the host and allocate no device memory: their honest peak is a measured zero, which the scorecard must tell from unmeasured. The verify is set when the ledger is built.

steps.title: Make recipe measure run the model instead of recovering a stored stage
steps.rationale: Measured 2026-10-03 (hermetic check, two identical single-stage executions: loads=2, runs=1): a run is keyed on recipe and request (capabilityruntime/run_key.go:13-15) and a stage whose receipt is complete is recovered from the store (workflowruntime/runtime.go:481,529-587); recipe measure runs the verification's own request under the same recipe, so for forecast, tabular, image-embedding, generation and transcription the measured attempt loads the model and returns the stored output, and for vqa it returns the stored answer without loading (RxBrain vqa first-output 135 ms against a 6.6 s training load). First-output on those rows is load plus replay, not what a user waits for. Decide the smallest honest form: a measure run that never recovers a stage. Parked finding 'recipe measure replays outputs' is this. The verify is a test that a measured attempt of a single-stage capability runs its node.

steps.title: Give the rows with no serving attempt a producer the cycle runs
steps.rationale: Six rows have no completed serving attempt. Fractale generation: cmd/validate/surfaces.go kindValidation has no generation case, so no cell. granite and nemotron transcription and webssl image-embedding: the command is bound and their verifications retain runnable requests, but the cell is current by its acceptance receipt, so nothing schedules recipe measure (one manual run fills them; validate-currency's every-cell cycle keeps them filled). Qwen3.8-27B and gemma-4-E4B projection: a projection capability has no executor, so recipe measure refuses it; its proof re-verifies and publishes no attempt, and E4B's producer publishes observations a gate depends on, which the scorecard excludes. Qwen2.5-0.5B training: trainingworkflow/heldout_run.go records no load phase where its sibling routes do. The verify is set per producer as each is built.

items.title: Delete validate's remaining per-cell currency once re-acquiring every cell is cheap

steps.title: Delete validate's remaining per-cell currency once re-acquiring every cell is cheap
steps.rationale: Stage 2 of evaluation-replay/delete-selection (scratchpad delete-selection.md, measured 2026-10-02). What goes: surfaces.go except kindValidation (about -130), the Reuse/Unknown buckets and refusal cases of SelectValidation (-30), acceptedRecords.current and readAcceptedRecords down to grounding and benchmark record binding (-80), recordCurrent/judgeBound/boundKey (-60, a 12-line bindBenchmark keeps protocol, cost and -replay), guard_records.go (-79) with cmd/longform's latest-records verb (-60), media_receipt.go (-111; it runs a real-model go test inside every dry run, about 1-1.5 min per validate call, while the models lane runs the same acceptances every cycle), and the inventory's validated standing (-35): about -550 production lines in cmd/validate and -400 test lines. What it costs: every activated applicable cell runs every cycle, about 2h10 of blocking cells in steady state against today's mean of about 1h, plus less device time for the background fill. Cuts that bring it toward the bar: Unlimited-OCR decodes at 3.9 tok/s, under 1% of its bandwidth bound, and its guard alone takes 11m43 (finding 870a92db); one evaluate process per model for its blocking families saves about 8 min of fixed overhead (measure before adding code); the 9B hybrid training proof (22m05, same cmd/train route and code as the blocking 4B proof) could run in the background, which is decision nine-b-proof-background. Even with all three about 1h40 remains, since guards, serving and media have no cheaper form. Re-measure the steady-state every-cell cost from the first cycle after delete-selection lands and land this when it is within an hour of today's cycles, or on the owner's word. Hazard this row must close (cycle 6, 2026-10-03): a published scorecard labels every cell with the publishing commit, whatever commit its record ran at. A held-out cell that enters a baseline while its record is stale there (a retained contract first listed by new code, or a background fill's record made at the previous measured commit) is later re-measured and compared across a range wider than main..candidate, so drift main already holds withholds the candidate: gemma-4-12B-it-fp8-native's raw mmlu-pro baseline 0.285488697 was a record 115 runtime commits older than main. Re-acquiring every compared cell at the published commit (replay making that cheap) removes the case; until then a baseline cell's value is only as fresh as its record.

items.title: Narrow the inference surface one responsibility at a time

steps.title: Keep non-text capability edits out of the inference surface
steps.rationale:
internal/modelrecipe is itself a surface root and holds every capability's tables, so a capability edit expires every text model's guard (e7ee897a expired nine; dinov2-embedding-capability did it again). Measured 2026-09-23: the split (a capabilityrecipe package modelrecipe does not import, with the text path compiling against a text-only catalog) renames symbols in 79 files, several on pinned media runtime paths, so it waits on reviewed-delta-registry. It still cannot keep a NEW task off the surface: recipe/schema.go (task constants, validateTask) and recipecontract/modality.go stay reachable from inference. Adding RAE's modules would be protected; adding a task would not. Re-measure 2026-09-27 after gate-small-cutover: the gate's own records drive most store growth and evidence churn, so this row may no longer be needed.

Serves: loop speed. Disappears: guard expirations caused by non-text edits, so fewer hour-long landings. Evidence: inferencesurface.Moves on each landing's diff. Batch: surface (the last one it causes).

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): all.

Re-scoped 2026-09-30 (owner review): narrow the surface incrementally, one concrete responsibility per change, each moved to its existing owner:
- composition's graft training;
- densecausal's training half;
- modelrecipe's dataset responsibility, to dataset;
- the capability tables.
Each change verifies three things separately: preserved behaviour (its tests), the build and test closure, and the surface invalidation (inferencesurface.Moves on its diff). Guards are re-acquired once after the last of a run of these. Measured 2026-09-30 (change 1 built, graft training moved to trainingworkflow; patch surface1.patch in the master-lead scratchpad): it takes only capabilityruntime and jsonabbrev out of the closure (69 to 67 packages). densecausal, trainingprogram and trainingdata stay because composition/chain.go, the Tier-0 chain probe, uses densecausal's forward half. So change 2 is the chain probe, not densecausal's training half: moving it to its owner drops 8 more packages (agenttool, densecausal, devicemath, hfbpe, operation, trainingdata, trainingprogram, workflowruntime). Moving candidate realization too drops bridgetrain, hostoptimizer and optimizer. Then modelrecipe's dataset responsibility and the capability tables. runrecord/generation.go:59's comment still names composition.RecordViability; fix it in the batch that reaches thoughtbank and integration anyway.

Measured 2026-09-30, not landed (patch surface5.patch in the master-lead scratchpad):
- In September, 8 of 153 surface moves came only through modelrecipe's capability tables. RAE 9f5ea65be, the linear entries dde56a6a2 and e7ee897a9, speech-assemble 674f096ee, VQA 1a2da932b, and the audio builders a2df8940b, d68490754 and 6d85fc6b6. Each cost a guard re-acquisition.
- A cut is blocked because candidate_recipe_derivation.go (production code in modelrecipe) calls CapabilityDefinition, and many binaries link modelrecipe without linking mediacapability. So moving a table out needs either registration at init in the owner package, or the 79-file split.
- The built cut registers only RAE's image-gen modules from internal/rae at init (+38 nodes). It covers 1 of 7 generation families, and it adds a second way to declare a capability beside the tables. That is not landed, per the owner's subtraction-first review.
- Options with costs:
  (1) Every image and video family through one registration seam: about 45 files, including pinned media paths that need reviewed deltas (latentimage and sensenovarecipe runtime_cuda_windows.go, latentvideo production.go, diffusionimage and oscillatorimage runtime.go, sensenovarecipe activate.go).
  (2) A task-keyed seam for linear capabilities: image embedding is about 40 lines; forecast and generation fixtures hit import cycles in 12 test packages.
  (3) Audio builders: renames in about 21 files, no pinned paths.
  (4) New tasks stay on the surface through recipe/schema.go and recipecontract/modality.go whatever is done.
- Recommendation: take this step only as (1) plus (3) in one registration mechanism that replaces the tables, not beside them, when the next non-text capability lands anyway. Until then, the 8 moves a month cost guard re-acquisitions that are batched once per run.

items.title: Move the remaining models out of adaptive_new and drop the test variables that point there

Owner recommendation 2026-09-27. Once goldens lock the ports, move the remaining models under adaptive_new/models (Wan, the Gemma configs) into overgo/models as TabFM was, and drop the test environment variables that point there: fewer outside paths, fewer environment-dependent skips and flakes. OWNER PERMISSION needed for the moves: the guard protects model directories.

From simplify-checkpoint-locations, retired 2026-09-29: move a checkpoint out of adaptive_new only where a live dependency on the retired root remains; verify the staged copy (hash, servable identity, baseline lookup, bounded inference, rollback) before switching locators; keep the original; no model vanishes.

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): the lanes of the packages whose tests move. From goldens-own-parity (closed 2026-09-30): the reference comparisons that remain (cmd/vqaparity, most of internal/adaptiveparity, the rest of cmd/sensenovaparity) stay because their goldens live outside git, in adaptive_new fixtures and store captures. Committing those goldens and pointing the kept tests at them is what lets those packages go; a provenance manifest would not. Never-run tests found on the way, each gated on a variable or tag nothing sets: TestGemma4FP8Leadership (OVERGO_GEMMA4_BASELINE), TestInferenceTextAndStructuredEvidenceIdentity, the modeltest process-peak tests, cmd/vqaparity TestRxBrainProductionParity, sensenovarecipe's SeededLatent and FullGeneration tests, and projector TestGemma4Real* and TestQwen3VLRealFixture. Each goes into a lane that sets its gate, or is deleted if a running test covers it. Also never run (2026-09-30): internal/adaptiveparity's experiment probes (TestComponentCompositionViability, TestTier0ChainViability, TestTier0ChainDoseResponse, TestBridgeSynthesisProducesEvidenceOrRefusal, TestAdapterRetrialProbe) sit behind OVERGO_PROBE_TEST, which no lane sets, and need Carbon-500M or MiniCPM5-1B, which are not registered on the master-lead machine. items.title: Carry the VAE lane's latent campaign surface until the lane closes it

steps.title: Carry the VAE lane's latent campaign surface until the lane closes it
steps.rationale: The overgo_vae lane (branch codex/overgo_vae, campaign overgo_rsi_with_vae, design docs/overgo_rsi_with_vae.md) runs the native-Go latent RSI and PEARL campaign with its own plan in its own worktree. Owner decision 2026-09-25: master takes the lane in parts that have a production consumer, not whole. Master ported the runtime part at e1ee1326fe2b (row vae-codec-stream-port: media.CodecChunkStream owning causal codec state, the Wan VAE host and CUDA encode and CUDA decode through it; the host streaming DecodeLatentVideo stays a test on master until it has a production caller); the ported files are byte-identical to the lane's, so merging master back is clean. DIRECTION FOR THE LANE when it merges master (master is in a consolidation-only phase: two birds with one stone, minimize to the maximum practical extent, no ledger where construction can prevent the object): (1) consumer first -- land each latent contract (representation latent state and codec, geometry, tensorstats resampling and robust scalars, media latent volume) together with its first production consumer; the first merge unit is first-latent-capability/existing-vae-inference-proof, and no export arrives without a caller; (2) no new record families -- express experimental evidence through the shared record table that automation-one-record-table builds instead of runrecord experimental_* families, and keep campaign-history adoption out of master's internal/plan; (3) reconcile pinned media runtime moves with a reviewed delta in docs/media_reviewed_deltas.json backed by a device receipt, never by narrowing TestReviewedDeltaRegistryExplainsTheTree; (4) never raise docs/clone_baseline.json -- the merged tree measured 7964 against master's 7991 while the lane raised it to 9970; (5) after merging master, drop the lane's testCodecChunkState copy in internal/media/codec_latent_test.go: master's TestCodecChunkStreamOwnsCausalState owns it; (6) keep evidence identities in compatibility.json refreshed from master's store, not the lane's. Master keeps its plan; any staged surface a later merge brings retires with this row. Done when the lane's campaign closeout has merged and TestVAECampaignClosedOut proves no staged entry names this row.

Re-pointing them fails six acceptance tests ('completion acceptance evidence does not match the plan authority'), and nothing in the tree produces these gate records: formatCompletionAcceptanceEvidence has no non-test caller. The re-pointing is built in the scratchpad's compatfold-repoint.patch (new digests: text-vision 62ebc6e5..., image-video 6bf91882...). It applies together with re-acquired records once a producer exists, or the proofs retire against a replacement that covers their contract. Deferred 2026-10-02 below the rows that can progress: the census needs the owner's review of the 11 identities the live catalog adds (snapshot 209, live 220), and re-acquiring the accepted baselines with realized residency needs the GPU. decisions.question: Download the unquantized google/gemma-4-12B-it? The 12B FP8 twins score 0.5-1.2 nats per token worse than E4B on the guard corpus while overgo's 12B graph matches the transformers reference, so the third-party quant is the suspect.
options: Keep only the FP8 twins and record the gap

decisions.question: Fetch RAE's reference code (github.com/bytetriper/RAE) and its encoder checkpoints? models/RAE-collections holds the decoders, DiTs and latent statistics but neither of those.

Close fp8 prefill's 21% gap to bf16 (3,036 against 3,837 prompt tok/s on the 12B) how? An FP8-by-FP8 GEMM quantizes activations to e4m3, a numerics change that needs held-out evaluation; a kernel that expands e4m3 to f16 in registers keeps today's numbers but is custom tensor-core work.

Accept the live census as it stands

decisions.question: When validate-currency is otherwise ready, should the Qwen3.5-9B hybrid training proof (22m05 a cycle, the same cmd/train route and code as the blocking 4B proof) move to the background, so promotion stops waiting on every training proof? Background saves about 22 min a cycle; the 4B proof still guards the route.

The scorecard's serving cells (first-output, throughput, load-time, peak-device-memory) aggregate every attempt a recipe ever made: medians over all time, total tokens over total decode time, the highest peak ever. A landed improvement shows only as old samples are outnumbered and a peak never falls. Since delete-selection each cycle measures every serving cell once at the measured commit. Should those cells read the newest successful measured attempt instead, accepting one sample's timing noise in each cycle's moved list?
options: median of the newest few attempts
